name: ai.navad/jobs
title: Navad
description: Search verified remote jobs free, and tailor resumes and cover letters with your Navad account.

tools.name: search_jobs
tools.description: Search Navad's remote job listings by keyword, location, seniority, salary, and recency. Returns summaries without full descriptions — call get_job for a specific posting's description. Free; no account needed. Always cite the returned `url` when telling the user about a job.

query.description: Keyword search across job title and description.

location.description: Regions or countries a candidate may work from, e.g. ["Europe", "Portugal"]. Call list_job_locations first for valid values. "Worldwide" means genuinely global, not "remote within one country".

min_salary.description: Lower bound on the maximum advertised salary.

posted_within_days.description: Only jobs posted in the last N days.

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Fetch one job posting in full, including its description. Accepts either the job's UUID or its URL slug. Free; no account needed.

job_id.description: The job's UUID or its URL slug. Both are accepted.

tools.name: list_job_locations
tools.description: List the regions and countries that can be passed to search_jobs `location`. Call this before filtering by location rather than guessing values.

tools.name: get_related_jobs
tools.description: Given a job UUID, find similar postings. Useful for widening a search after the user shows interest in one role.

job_id.description: UUID of the job to find similar postings for.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Show how much of this month's AI allowance is left, per feature. Call this before running several AI tools in a row, and to explain a limit error rather than retrying into it.

tools.name: list_my_resumes
tools.description: List the user's stored résumés and their IDs. Call this before start_apply_with_ai, which requires a resume_id. Does not return file contents or download links.

tools.name: get_job_ai_tools
tools.description: For one job, report which AI artifacts already exist (tailored résumé, cover letter, interview prep, ATS score). Costs nothing. Use it to avoid regenerating something the user already has, and to retrieve a result after a generation tool timed out.

tools.name: tailor_resume
tools.description: Rewrite the user's résumé for a specific job. Uses one unit of the monthly résumé allowance. Takes 30–120 seconds. Returns the tailored résumé text — show it to the user and refine it with them in conversation rather than regenerating, since each call costs another unit. If you also want a cover letter and ATS score, call start_apply_with_ai instead: it runs in the background and cannot time out.

resume_id.description: Which stored résumé to use. Omit to use the default. Call list_my_resumes to see the options.

force.description: Regenerate even if a result already exists, or if the match score is low. Spends allowance. Only set this when the user asks.

tools.name: write_cover_letter
tools.description: Write a cover letter for a specific job from the user's résumé. Uses one unit of the monthly cover-letter allowance. Takes 30–120 seconds. Returns the letter text — refine it with the user in conversation rather than regenerating. If one already exists for this job it is returned without spending allowance.

resume_id.description: Which stored résumé to use. Omit to use the default. Call list_my_resumes to see the options.

force.description: Regenerate even if a result already exists, or if the match score is low. Spends allowance. Only set this when the user asks.

tools.name: check_ats_score
tools.description: Score how well a résumé will pass the applicant tracking system for a specific job. Returns the score plus the per-category breakdown, keyword analysis, and concrete fixes. Uses one unit of the monthly ATS allowance. Pass generated_resume_id to score a tailored résumé rather than a stored one.

resume_id.description: Which stored résumé to use. Omit to use the default. Call list_my_resumes to see the options.

force.description: Regenerate even if a result already exists, or if the match score is low. Spends allowance. Only set this when the user asks.

generated_resume_id.description: Score a tailored résumé produced by tailor_resume instead of a stored one.

tools.name: prepare_interview
tools.description: Generate likely interview questions, suggested answers, company research, and weak spots for a specific job, and return them so you can run a mock interview with the user. PREMIUM PLAN ONLY — on Free and Pro this returns a limit error prompting an upgrade, so check get_usage first if unsure.

resume_id.description: Which stored résumé to use. Omit to use the default. Call list_my_resumes to see the options.

force.description: Regenerate even if a result already exists, or if the match score is low. Spends allowance. Only set this when the user asks.

tools.name: start_apply_with_ai
tools.description: Start a background run producing a tailored résumé, a cover letter, and an ATS score for one job. Preferred over calling the individual tools when the user wants more than one artifact: it returns immediately and cannot time out. Spends allowance across each requested feature. Returns an application_run_id to poll.

job_id.description: UUID of the job posting to apply to.

resume_id.description: Required here (unlike the single-artifact tools). Call list_my_resumes first.

tools.name: get_application_run_status
tools.description: Poll a run started by start_apply_with_ai. Report per-stage state, not just the overall status — a run can finish 'completed' with one stage failed, and that is normal.

application_run_id.description: The id returned by start_apply_with_ai. Not a job posting id.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Read the signed-in user's name, plan, and job-search preferences (desired roles, seniority, skills, salary, locations). Use this before searching so results reflect what they actually want, and to explain why a posting does or does not match. No allowance is spent.

tools.name: update_profile
tools.description: Change the user's display name. Requires a token with profile access. Only call this when the user explicitly asks — never to 'correct' a name you think looks wrong.

tools.name: update_job_preferences
tools.description: Change the preferences that drive job matching — desired roles, seniority, skills, salary range, locations, timezone flexibility. Only the fields you pass are changed. Requires a token with profile access. Read them with get_profile first and confirm the change with the user before writing.

desired_roles.description: Job titles to match on, e.g. ["Backend Engineer"].

experience_level.description: Seniority, e.g. "senior". Call get_profile to see the current value.

preferred_locations.description: Regions or countries, e.g. ["Europe"]. See list_job_locations.

tools.name: start_cv_upload
tools.description: Get a short-lived URL to upload a PDF CV to. The file does NOT pass through this tool — you upload the bytes yourself with an HTTP PUT, then call finish_cv_upload. Requires a token with profile access, and a client that can read local files. If you cannot do that, send the user to their profile page instead of guessing.

tools.name: finish_cv_upload
tools.description: Complete a CV upload started by start_cv_upload, after the bytes have been PUT to the upload URL. The server verifies the file really is a PDF here, so a failure at this step usually means the upload did not land.

label.description: A name for this CV, e.g. "Backend CV".

file_size.description: Size of the uploaded file in bytes.
